2607.02473.title: Audio-Based Understanding of Audiobook Narration Appeal
2607.02473.paper_summary: Narration is central to the audiobook listening experience, shaping how listeners engage with and understand the content. This work explores how narration qualities shape an audiobook's appeal, noting that their effects can vary by genre, title, and audience. We extract vocal and acoustic features (e.g., tone, pace, loudness) from LibriVox using pre-trained audio models and analyse their relationship with consumption data (specifically, view-rate) and their interplay with genre and title. Despite limited consumption data, we find that acoustic information alone has a robust association with appeal, even after accounting for title effects. We further validate these findings using more nuanced proprietary engagement metrics. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic computational study linking narration qualities, genre, title, and audiobook consumption, highlighting the potential of data-driven insights to improve audiobook personalisation and narrator casting.
2607.02473.paper_summary_zh: 敘述對於有聲書的聆聽體驗至關重要，塑造了聽眾如何與內容互動和理解內容。這項工作探討了敘述特質如何影響有聲書的吸引力，並指出其效果可能因類型、標題和受眾而異。 我們從LibriVox提取聲音和聲學特徵（例如，音調、節奏、音量），並分析它們與消費數據（具體而言，觀看率）之間的關係，以及它們與類型和標題的相互作用。 儘管消費數據有限，我們發現僅聲學信息與吸引力之間有著強烈的關聯，即使在考慮標題效應之後。我們進一步使用更細緻的專有參與度指標來驗證這些發現。 據我們所知，這是第一個系統性的計算研究，將敘述特質、類型、標題和有聲書消費聯繫起來，突顯了數據驅動的見解在改善有聲書個性化和旁白選角方面的潛力。
